title: Isaac favors Esau, Rebekah favors Jacob — Genesis 25
paragraphs: Isaac favors Esau, Rebekah favors Jacob — Genesis 25

Isaac loved Esau.
Rebekah loved Jacob.
And one broken home became a battlefield before the blessing ever came.

Genesis 25 does not hide the wound.
“Isaac loved Esau… but Rebekah loved Jacob” (Genesis 25:28).

That one verse explains so much.
Favoritism does not stay quiet.
It grows in kitchens.
It hardens in glances.
It teaches brothers to compete instead of love.

Esau became the father’s favorite because of appetite and skill.
Jacob became the mother’s favorite because of closeness and preference.
And the family started splitting long before the deception in Genesis 27.

This is not just a story about bad parenting.
This is a mirror.

Homes still break when love is uneven.
Children still bleed when approval is selective.
Parents still shape rivalry when affection is louder for one than another.
And sin always turns preference into pain.

Yet even in that fractured house, God was not defeated.
Human favoritism could not cancel divine purpose.
Messy people still stood inside the plan of God.

That is the scandal of grace.
God works through broken families without calling their brokenness good.
And that points us to Jesus.

Because where earthly families fail, Christ does not.
He is the better Son, the better Brother, the better Savior.
He does not love with partiality.
He does not withhold grace from the weak.
He invites the wounded, the overlooked, the angry, and the ashamed to come and be made new.

So if you grew up fighting for love…
If you were compared, neglected, or pushed aside…
Hear this clearly:

Your worth was never decided by who favored you.
Your identity is settled at the cross.
In Christ, you are not the leftover child.
You are seen. Wanted. Redeemed.
